questions.q: What does an offline backup of Neo4j actually involve, and which editions support it?
options: Stopping the database and copying its data directory directly — available in every edition, including Community
Running neo4j-admin database backup against a live instance — Enterprise only
Offline backups are not possible in Neo4j at all
Offline backup only works in Neo4j Aura
questions.explain: The stop-copy-start pattern is the universal fallback available even on Community Edition, at the cost of requiring downtime.

questions.q: What is the real edition requirement for online, non-disruptive backup in Neo4j?
options: It's an Enterprise Edition feature — Community Edition cannot take a backup while the database is running
Online backup is available in every edition equally
Online backup requires Neo4j Aura specifically and no self-hosted edition supports it
Online backup was removed from Neo4j entirely and only offline backup exists now
questions.explain: neo4j-admin database backup against a running instance with no downtime is gated behind Enterprise Edition, the same way custom RBAC was in the previous lesson.

questions.q: What does the --from flag target when running neo4j-admin database backup?
options: The backup listen address of a running Neo4j instance — a dedicated port separate from the Bolt port applications connect through
The file path where the backup will be saved
The name of the database user performing the backup
The version of Neo4j the backup will be compatible with
questions.explain: Online backup runs over its own backup protocol and port, distinct from the Bolt port used for normal application connections.

questions.q: What does the --overwrite-destination=true flag on neo4j-admin database restore do, and why does it matter?
options: It explicitly permits replacing existing database files at the target path — a deliberate safeguard against silently clobbering a live database by accident
It compresses the restored database to save disk space
It automatically restarts the Neo4j server after restore completes
It has no real safety purpose and is just a legacy flag
questions.explain: This mirrors the same instinct as WITH REPLACE on a SQL Server RESTORE DATABASE statement — an explicit opt-in rather than a silent overwrite.

questions.q: What is the efficiency benefit of incremental backups in Neo4j Enterprise Edition?
options: Later backup runs against the same target only capture changes since the last backup, rather than a full copy every time — the same argument behind SQL Server differentials
Incremental backups eliminate the need for any full backup ever
Incremental backups are actually slower than full backups but more secure
Incremental backups are a Community Edition-only feature
questions.explain: This is the same efficiency tradeoff SQL Server differentials offer relative to repeated full backups.
